content.user_title: Define Art Direction Before Generating Assets
content.value_statement: Vague visual briefs lead to inconsistent assets and repeated generation costs. This skill guides style decisions, moodboard comparisons, palette constraints, and storyboard planning before production.
actual_capabilities: Translate vague style and era labels into concrete materials, textures, shapes, and production terms.
Plan moodboards that compare one visual axis while preserving the subject and palette.
Define palette constraints and prioritize value contrast for gameplay readability.
Specify camera height, distance, and framing as explicit visual decisions.
Structure storyboards around advancing narrative beats and choose combined boards or separate shot images.
Plan continuity through approved reference images and handoffs to related Layer skills.
limitations: Image generation, video animation, and timeline assembly depend on external Layer tools and related skills.
The skill provides guidance, not bundled scripts, models, or rendering assets.
Visual direction requires user feedback and approval before production.
Palette guidance does not provide automated contrast testing or accessibility certification.

use_cases.title: Establish a Game Asset Style
use_cases.description: Compare rendering styles for one hero prop, then define a shared palette and reference anchor for subsequent assets.

use_cases.title: Plan an Advertising Storyboard
use_cases.description: Write advancing narrative beats and specify framing for each panel before preparing separate images for animation.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Client Visual Brief
use_cases.description: Translate broad style labels into concrete visual choices and present a focused moodboard for client approval.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Visual Style
prompt_templates.prompt: My brief is [brief], and the desired style is [style word]. Ask about tone, then propose concrete production terms for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn a vague style label into a usable direction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Focused Moodboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan four moodboard directions for [subject]. Vary only [visual axis], preserve [palette], and describe the approval decision before generation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare visual directions without changing multiple variables.

prompt_templates.title: Define Palette and Framing
prompt_templates.prompt: For [game scene], define a constrained palette, gameplay value contrast, camera height, and shot distance. Keep [team colors] consistent across assets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: establish readable and repeatable scene decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Trailer Production Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a trailer for [game] using [approved direction]. Write advancing beats, separate storyboard panels, reference continuity, and handoffs for animation and assembly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect an approved direction to a multi-shot production plan.

output_examples.input: We need a retro robot style but have not chosen the look.
output: Proposed direction: matte plastic, saturated primary colors, rounded forms, and visible CRT details.
Moodboard: show the same robot in four rendering styles while holding its silhouette and palette constant.
Approval: select one rendering style before preparing further assets.

output_examples.input: Plan a three-shot trailer about a scout discovering an enemy fortress.
output: Beat 1: the scout reaches a ridge; use a medium-wide view at eye level.
Beat 2: the fortress comes into view; use a wide shot from behind the scout.
Beat 3: a searchlight reveals the scout; use a close view to establish the immediate threat.
Prepare three separate panel images with the approved reference anchor, then hand them off for image-to-video animation.

best_practices: Confirm concrete style terms and approve a direction before generating assets at volume.
Change one moodboard axis at a time and retain the selected image as a reference anchor.
Write advancing story beats first and create separate panels when each will become a video shot.
anti_patterns: Passing vague labels such as realistic or retro into prompts without defining their visual markers.
Changing subject, palette, and rendering style together in a comparison moodboard.
Relying only on hue differences to distinguish gameplay-critical elements.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides art direction; generation mechanics rely on Layer tools and related skills.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available Layer tools determine which production steps can run.

faq.question: What should a moodboard compare?
faq.answer: Compare one visual axis, such as rendering style, while keeping the subject and palette consistent.

faq.question: When should storyboard panels be separate images?
faq.answer: Use separate images when each panel will become an individual video shot or needs independent framing control.

faq.question: How does the skill address color readability?
faq.answer: It prioritizes value contrast for gameplay-critical elements and consistent colors where hue carries meaning.

faq.question: What happens when a related skill is missing?
faq.answer: It asks the user to install the missing skill. During unattended work, it proceeds from available tool schemas and flags the gap.
